newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Sovereign eyes on Japan, U.K.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Sovereign eyes on Japan, U.K.

text.p: With the dust barely settling on its jumbo 30-year global bond and 20-year Eurolira issue, Brazil is already sniffing out new-issue prospects in Japanese yen and pound sterling.
A Central Bank official, denying rumors on Friday that Brazil had decided to issue debt in the two currencies, said: "The only thing concrete is that we are interested."
The official said the Central Bank had received a report from Japanese consultants on issuing a Euroyen, but he added that the bank had not yet invited investment banks to bid.
He would not comment further on the sterling deal, but talk in the market points to a 10-year 200 million sterling ($320 million) bond.
THE PRIMARY MARKET THIS WEEK will again feature a number of Brazilian issues, which have dominated the emerging markets debt calendar the past two weeks.
* Eletrobras was expected to announce its lead manager for a $400 million 10-year bond and possibly price the deal this week. Market talk says Salomon Brothers may have won the deal.
* Banco Interatlantico was expected on Tuesday to price a $125 million three-year bond, said lead manager Indosuez. The bond is expected to have a spread of 200-225 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

* Banco Credito de Sao Paulo was also scheduled Tuesday to launch its $40 million eight-year step-up bond, lead manager WestMerchant bank said. The bank said pricing should come at a spread of 445-455 bps.
* Steelmaker CSN should launch its $300 million 10-year bullet bond via J.P. Morgan/NationsBank sometime this week. Market talk for the deal is about 280 bps.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, Brazilian Eurobonds widened 10 bps on average last week, making many of the issues attractive this week, traders said.
"We had a lot of new issues and people were getting out of old paper to get new issues," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo, explaining last week's wider spreads.
"But as people look closely at Brazilian Eurobonds, they are going to see good upside," the trader added.

Brazil's 8.875 percent global due 2001 looked like a good bargain at 163 bps over when compared to Argentina's 9.25 percent due 2001 ZN4D, which has tightened to the 135 bp range. Argentina's 2001 was trading tighter than even Mexico's 9.75 percent due 2001 ZM5W, now at about 140 bps.

Traders also said there was good demand for Grupo Votorantim's eight-year putable bond ZYHB, which was raised to $400 million from $300 million due to exceptional demand when it was priced last week. The bond was holding firm at about 202 bps over after pricing at 210.
The bond, Grupo Votorantim's first, is the largest-ever debt issue by a private Brazilian company, according to lead manager ING Bank.
